newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher in quiet trading on Thursday as the market awaited release of July's consumer price index (CPI) on Friday, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.09 pct to 111.26
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.1 pct to 111.55
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.09 pct to 110.39
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.04 pct at 110.8
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.12 pct to 108.82
Volume including Makams was a moderate 132 million shekels.

"The market is waiting to see what July's CPI will be. Prices of CPI-linked bonds rose today, basically as a correction to their falls in the past week," said a trader at a major institutional investor.

Prices of inflation-linked bonds had fallen over the past week on fears that a high July CPI would trigger an interest rate hike. But the trader said that as a result yields had again become attractive causing traders to buy on Thursday.
"Basically the yields of CPI-linked bonds have resumed their trend lower on the tight supply expected this month," the trader said.
Yields on CPI-linked bonds have fallen in the last two months to an average of 3.6 percent from 4.2 percent.

Economists are looking for a rise of 1.0 to 1.2 percent in July's CPI following a steep 1.1 percent increase in June. Traders fear another sharp rise will trigger an interest rate hike of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points at the end of the month.
The base rate has been 12.7 percent since the middle of June.
Morris Sebag of Sahar Securities said the cabinet's approval of the Treasury's the 1998 budget proposals on Wednesday night was another factor in boosting demand for CPI-linked bonds.
"Some of the uncertainty has been erased. The cuts are to bring the deficit down to 2.4 percent of gross domestic product, which signals that interest rates are not likely to soar," he said.
Ministers gave the go-ahead to slash 2.3 billion shekels from next year's 164.4 billion shekel budget.
Prices of unlinked bonds rose on Thursday after a major redemption by the government caused institutions to put excess liquidity into unlinked bonds, Sebag said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.53 shekels)
